newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-STRUGGLING STEAUA STUN LEADERS ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STRUGGLING STEAUA STUN LEADERS ATLETICO.

text.p: Strugglers Steaua Bucharest hit back to snatch an unexpected 1-1 draw against group B leaders Atletico Madrid in their European Cup Champions ' League match on Wednesday.

Forward Sabin Ilie scored six minutes after the break -- Steaua's first genuine goal in five league matches. Defender Daniel Bogusz of Poland's Widzew Lodz had contributed an own goal for the Romanians' benefit in an earlier game.
Atletico grabbed a 23rd minute lead when Francisco Narvaez sent a perfect cross from the right and Serb playmaker Milinko Pantic scored from an unmarked close-range position into an empty net.
Argentine forward Juan Esnaider nearly snatched a winner for the Spanish side well into the second half when he hit a post from inside the area.

Romanian fans were denied a last chance to see key striker Adrian Ilie, who had to pull out at the last minute through injury. He is moving to Galatasaray of Istanbul this weekend on a three year-contract.
Atletico are level on 10 points with Germany's Borussia Dortmund while Steaua are bottom of the group and have no chance of reaching the quarter-finals.
Steaua's trainer Dumitru Dumitriu said he was delighted his unfancied charges had managed gainst the powerful Spanish side.

"We deserved the victory but my players missed some good chances to score, especially in the first half," Atletico's Serb coach Radomir Antic said. "And it always happens that if you don't score, your opponents somehow manage to."
